proof_checks.argument: Symmetric diagonalization uses char(k) != 2; algebraic closure supplies finitely many square roots to normalize nonzero diagonal entries. Alternating normal form gives even rank and symplectic blocks. Rank(G) <= rank(f) <= m. Embed the canonical r-dimensional form into the nondegenerate ambient standard form and undo congruence by multiplying the tuple by S^{-1}. This realizes every allowed rank.

rank(G)=m forces rank(f)=m. Surjectivity and nondegeneracy identify ker(f) with ker(G); symmetry or skew-symmetry allows either pairing order. Equal Gram matrices yield the unique map T(f1(c))=f2(c), well-defined by the common kernel, invertible and form-preserving. Spanning tuples have trivial stabilizers. The full orthogonal group is essential; no SO orbit assertion is made.

Choose a coordinate complement to the kernel. Write K=graph(A) and q(x,y)=y-Ax. Then G=Q^T H Q, Q=(-A|I_r), with H invertible and symmetric/alternating. The inverse recovers H=G22 and A=-H^{-1}G21, regular on det(H) != 0. Some coordinate complement always exists, so the finitely many principal-block opens cover the stratum. The nondegenerate quotient and its dimension follow from radical/rank definitions and rank-nullity.

There are N=r(t-r)+r(r+1)/2 symmetric parameters or N=r(t-r)+r(r-1)/2 alternating parameters. Polynomial-ring dimension plus prime localization gives an upper bound N. The coordinate-prime flag translated through A=0,H=I_r or J_r avoids det(H), whose value there is 1, and gives lower bound N. The same bound holds for classical chains by closure/vanishing ideals and coordinate affine-subspace flags. Hilbert basis makes chart rings Noetherian; a finite chart cover is Noetherian, and the open-cover dimension lemma glues chart dimensions.

r=0 and t=0 give the zero matrix and dimension zero, with empty determinant 1; r=t has no kernel parameters. Odd alternating rank is excluded. If t<m the maximal-rank fiber claim is inapplicable. Basis choices, normal-form rescalings and coordinate flags are finite. Only the explicitly choice-free finite-generation implication of Hilbert basis is used; no arbitrary basis or prime-ideal existence via Zorn is needed.
